newsitem.title: USA: Penn Traffic says sale will lift Q4 EBITDA.
newsitem.headline: Penn Traffic says sale will lift Q4 EBITDA.

text.p: The Penn Traffic Co said Monday it has sold a land parcel near Columbus, Ohio, for net proceeds of about $8 million, with the income expected to give the company a pretax gain of roughly $1 million in the fourth quarter ending Feb 1.

The company, a food retailer in the eastern U.S., said it would announce its fourth quarter earnings and same-store sales Feb 12 and predicted its EBITDA performance would be the highest of any quarter this fiscal year, exceeding analyst estimates.
"The company estimates that EBITDA in the fourth quarter will be between $49 million and $52 million, including the aforementioned gain on the sale of real estate," it said in a press release.
EBITDA is earnings before interest, depreciation, amortization, LIFO provision, unusual items, extraordinary items, and cumulative effect of accounting principle and taxes.
The company said it was making its projection of fourth-quarter results "in light of certain unfounded speculation currently circulating about the company," without giving further details.

It said the sold land parcel is part of a long-term development of approximately 350 acres, adding Penn Traffic has been selling smaller parcels of land in the area for residential use since late 1995 and will continue to do so.
The purchaser will use a portion of the land to develop a shopping center to include a new Big Bear supermarket which the Penn Traffic expects to open in 1998, the company said.

Penn Traffic operates 266 supermarkets in Pennsylvania, upstate New York, Ohio and West Virginia under the "Big Bear", "Big Bear Plus", "Bi-Lo Foods", "Insalaco's", "P&C", "Quality Markets", and "Riverside" trade names.
